claims: The International Space Station (ISS) is the primary continuously inhabited space station in low-Earth orbit.
The ISS serves as a multinational laboratory.
The ISS serves as a home for astronauts.
The ISS orbits at roughly 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h).
The ISS orbits Earth every 90 minutes.
The ISS has a 25-year history of international collaboration.
China operates the separate Tiangong space station.
The ISS has a bright fast-moving appearance in the sky.
Long-term exposure to microgravity causes bone/muscle loss.
The ISS serves as a laboratory for experiments in biology physics and astronomy.
The ISS tests technology for long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.
The ISS is approximately the size of a soccer field including solar arrays.
The ISS consists of modules from five different space agencies.
NASA Spot the Station app provides real-time tracking flyover schedules and alerts for the ISS.
NASA Spot the Station website provides real-time tracking flyover schedules and alerts for the ISS.
